findings.title: Percentage parsing ignores the full numeric value
findings.body: The unanchored regex extracts only the first unsigned decimal substring. Consequently, `-25%` returns `0.25` instead of `-0.25`, `1e2%` returns `0.01` instead of `1`, and `.5%` returns `0.05` instead of `0.005`. It also accepts junk such as `abc25%`, while `%` crashes because `match()` returns null. This can silently produce incorrect rates or terminate callers.
findings.recommendation: Convert and validate the entire substring before `%` rather than extracting digits, preserving Number-compatible signs and numeric forms while handling an invalid or empty prefix without throwing.

next_steps: Correct full-prefix percentage parsing and verify signed, leading-decimal, exponent, junk, and empty-prefix cases.
